summary.text: Barr has said AI could fundamentally transform the economy and society, with long-run benefits but possible short-term labor-market disruption and harm to some workers. He has argued that capturing AI's benefits requires managing risks, including bias in consumer lending and deepfake-enabled fraud. Barr has described the Federal Reserve as having established an AI program and governance framework and as using GenAI tools where appropriate within clear guardrails. He has said policy choices in areas such as education, worker training, competition, and tax policy will help determine whether AI's gains are broadly shared.

statements.text: Artificial intelligence (AI)—and by this, I mean in particular the recent explosive growth of generative AI—looks increasing likely to become what technologists call a general-purpose technology.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Financial institutions, and the Federal Reserve System, should consider investing sufficient resources in understanding GenAI technology, incorporating it into their workflows where appropriate, and training staff on how to use the technology responsibly and effectively.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Meanwhile, the financial regulatory community should approach the changing landscape with agility and flexibility.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: And beyond the financial sector, collaboration between governments, private industry, and research institutions will be critical to ensure that GenAI systems are not weaponized in catastrophic ways.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: We should continue to focus on responsible AI research and development and implement safeguards against misuse, including monitoring systems, standards for secure AI system development, and agreement on red lines for acceptable use cases.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Another thing I want to emphasize is AI governance. I think most would agree that the goal of the technology is to improve the human condition, and to do that, we need to be intentional in advancing that goal.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: We should make sure that we think about GenAI as enhancing, not replacing, humans, and set up best practices and cultural norms to that end.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: In the realm of regulation, frameworks for understanding model risk may need to be updated to address the complexity and challenges of explaining AI methods and the difficulty of assessing data quality.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Every financial institution should recognize the limitations of the technology, explore where and when GenAI belongs in any process, and identify how humans can be best positioned to be in the loop.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Today, I will address that question by outlining two hypothetical scenarios for AI's impact and the implications for businesses, regulators, and society.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: I will focus my comments on Generative AI, or GenAI, a subset of AI that has seen significant growth and integration into economic activity in just a few short years.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: GenAI will likely become a "general purpose technology," with widespread adoption, continuous improvement, and productivity enhancements to a wide range of sectors across the economy.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Thinking through hypothetical scenarios can help widen our lens to a range of possible outcomes and provide a framework for assessing the balance between benefits and risks.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Scenarios are not predictions of the future, but provide a framework for analyzing the factors that could lead to different outcomes.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: In the short term, GenAI may be overhyped, while in the long run, it may be underappreciated.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: If AI agents proliferate in financial transactions, we will also need to be careful about the potential for unintended consequences such as collusion among AI agents.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: To get prepared for this moment, bank risk managers and regulators should become familiar with Gen AI trends and monitor developments outside the bank perimeter so that they are not caught off guard as this technology quickly enters the banking system.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Fintech developers should, for example, prioritize identifying biases in training data sets and monitoring outputs in order to prevent those biases from amplifying inequalities or mispricing risks.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: They should review and update existing standards on model risk management, as appropriate, and engage in public–private forums where there are opportunities to work together.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Now, advances in AI can do much more damage by replicating a person's entire identity. This technology—known as deepfakes—has the potential to supercharge identity fraud.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: As we consider this issue from a policy perspective, we need to take steps to make attacks less likely by raising the cost of the attack to the cybercriminals and lowering the costs of defense to financial institutions and law enforcement.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: To the extent deepfakes increase, bank identity verification processes should evolve in kind to include AI-powered advances such as facial recognition, voice analysis, and behavioral biometrics to detect potential deepfakes.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Regulators should consider how we could leverage AI technologies ourselves, including to enhance our ability to monitor and detect patterns of fraudulent activity at regulated institutions in real time.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Another way to disrupt the economics of cybercrime is by increasing penalties for attempting to use Gen AI to commit fraud and increasing investment in cybercrime enforcement.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: The fear of severe legal consequences could help to deter bad actors from pursuing AI-driven fraud schemes in the first place.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Attackers can also turn to "dark web" tools, such as jailbroken versions of popular large language models, where the guardrails have been removed, to learn the deepfake trade and improve their attacks.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: AI is poised to transform our economy, likely in profound ways. But the speed and extent of that transformation are not yet clear. AI is likely to boost productivity, increase scientific discovery, and transform the nature of work. How these developments unfold will have important implications for society and for central bankers.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Meanwhile, we will also be closely monitoring how technologies like artificial intelligence are being integrated into economic activity and analyzing the implications for how the economy will evolve.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: AI holds enormous promise of faster economic growth, advances in human health, and a higher standard of living. But alongside the kinds of labor market disruptions seen in past episodes of revolutionary technological change, we will need to consider the possibility of more sweeping changes in the way we work.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Like past waves of information technology, AI will substitute for human labor in some tasks, complement human labor in other tasks, and spur the creation of new tasks that humans will perform, at least initially.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: In scenario 1, the issues that society has to address will be more straightforward. Policymakers will have to decide how to regulate emergent technologies, education and training programs will have to be tailored to shifts in labor demand, and some labor market regulations may need to be updated.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: In scenario 2, the issues that society will need to address will be more profound. Questions will include how to ensure that the economic gains associated with AI are broadly shared across individuals and households, and how to adapt social institutions to a world in which many more individuals in their prime working years may be working less.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: As a central banker, I can speak more specifically about how structural changes in the economy related to AI could affect monetary policy considerations—in particular, the Federal Reserve's dual mandate to promote maximum employment and stable prices.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: AI may require monetary policymakers to reassess our estimates of the natural rate of unemployment, which informs our assessment of the cyclical state of the economy and thus the appropriate stance of monetary policy.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: In my remarks, I would like to address a key question facing economists, policymakers, and people all over the world: How will artificial intelligence, particularly generative artificial intelligence, or GenAI, affect workers and the labor market in the years ahead?

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Growing evidence indicates that AI will be a "general purpose technology"—such as railroads, electricity, or computers—which is characterized by widespread adoption, complementary progress in many downstream applications, and ongoing improvement in the core technology.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Unlike traditional machine learning techniques, which often focus on relatively simple prediction and classification tasks, the large language models that have emerged in recent years can generate new content—anything from news articles to computer code to images and video to customer service dialogue. Emerging forms of "agentic" AI can undertake complex, multistep tasks—for example, taking a customer through a transaction and then placing an automated order.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: The net effects of AI on employment, both in the aggregate and across demographic and education groups, will depend on the relative size of these offsetting effects.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: AI has the potential to fundamentally change the economy and society. And as central bankers, we need to keep up.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: My view is that GenAI is a transformative technology that central banks need to remain engaged with to ensure an ability to execute as technology evolves.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: At the Federal Reserve, we have focused on ensuring we can leverage AI capabilities by establishing an AI program and governance framework for the use of AI technologies.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: As we push ahead on efficiency gains, it is important that we leverage the right tools for the task at hand, recognizing that GenAI is not always the best choice.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: To successfully leverage the potential of GenAI on a sustainable basis, decisions based on those models must be well controlled, numerically and legally precise, explainable, and replicable.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: We need to reduce the risk that AI reinforces biases in consumer lending. And we also need to guard against the risks that could result from the use of AI in financial markets.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: That is why the Federal Reserve is using AI, where appropriate, to increase staff efficiency and effectiveness.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: As with other general-purpose technologies, the long-run effects of AI are likely to be profoundly positive. But in the short term, AI may deeply disrupt labor markets and harm some workers.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: The speed of AI adoption may be much faster than previous general-purpose technologies, boosting productivity growth, but also allowing less time for workers, businesses, and the economy to adapt to these changes.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Within the Federal Reserve System, we have also been exploring the use of AI in our own operations and have established an AI program and governance framework for the use of AI technologies.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Within clear guardrails, we are using GenAI tools to translate legacy code, generate unit tests, and accelerate cloud migration.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: In my judgement, now is the time for society to begin to consider how to address these potential disruptions, while AI adoption is in its early stages.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: As a central banker, I see endeavoring to understand how AI is evolving and affecting labor markets as a crucial component of our work in the years ahead.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: For all of these reasons, I expect that the AI boom is unlikely to be a reason for lowering policy rates.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: But in the short term, AI may deeply disrupt labor markets and harm some workers. The ultimate impact on workers will depend not only on the extent of the disruption and the length of time it takes for the long-term benefits to appear, but importantly on how we, as a society, navigate this transition.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: AI models, on the other hand, learn by example: An AI model doesn't need to be told exactly how to accomplish a certain task, only provided with the right training data to infer patterns.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Consequently, AI can learn how to complete complex, nonroutine tasks that require knowledge that is difficult or impossible for humans to codify.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Moreover, agentic AI can accomplish more general goals with limited human supervision, mimicking human decision-making, reasoning, and implementation.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: The capabilities of GenAI models have improved rapidly. In just a few years, we have seen AI models meet or surpass human performance on increasingly challenging benchmarks, including competition-level mathematics and Ph.D.-level science questions.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: A central question is whether AI will expand opportunity by giving more people access to valuable skills and productive work, or whether it will reinforce advantages that are already concentrated among a smaller population.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: At one extreme, competition and distributed innovation could lead to AI becoming a cheap and ubiquitous commodity. In this scenario, access is democratized and gains are widely shared.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: As a result of these forces, it is possible that a small number of AI firms may dominate the market and investment returns may accrue primarily to owners of AI.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Just as the printing press democratized knowledge and the internet democratized information, AI may democratize capability itself.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Decisions on AI policy, education, worker training and workforce development, competition, tax policy, and other areas will help determine this outcome.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: The question I would like to consider today is whether AI will likely help narrow inequalities of income and wealth, supporting advances in financial inclusion, or widen those inequalities, undermining the recent gains in financial inclusion that we rightly celebrate today.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: First, AI could lead to labor displacement. Something that is at the top of mind for most people, especially younger workers, is the concern that AI could drastically reduce the demand for them.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: But in this scenario, AI could harm not only less-skilled workers, but also younger college-educated workers whose skills are more easily replicated by AI than in prior technological waves.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: AI might disproportionately affect new entrants to the labor market.

attribution.speaker: Michael S. Barr
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.
